samples.question: This picture contains exactly one large square panel with a solid dark border, exactly three much narrower upright slats that also have solid dark borders, and a few tiny dark specks on the background that are decoration only. The panel's border encloses a seven-by-seven grid of forty-nine equal square cells, that is seven columns of seven cells each. Four of those columns are drawn as bars: in such a column the lowest cells are dark, in the same tone as the border, and the cells above them are pale, in the same tone as the panel's background, so the column shows a solid bar standing on the panel's bottom edge whose height is a whole number of cells from 1 to 7. The other three columns are empty slots: all seven of their cells are filled with a single intermediate tone, neither the dark bar tone nor the pale background tone, and those three empty slots are either the three leftmost columns or the three rightmost columns of the panel. Each of the three narrow slats encloses one single column of seven cells, drawn at the same cell size as the panel and carrying one bar of its own, standing on the slat's bottom edge, in the same two tones. The three slats are the missing columns of the panel. Carry out this operation. Take the three slats in top-to-bottom order of their positions in the picture, take the panel's three empty slots in left-to-right order, and put the topmost slat's bar into the leftmost empty slot, the middle slat's bar into the middle empty slot, and the bottommost slat's bar into the rightmost empty slot, each bar keeping its own height and standing on the panel's bottom edge. The panel now has seven bars, and their seven heights, read left to right, form exactly one of these four symbols. 'ramp' is heights 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. 'crest' is heights 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 6, 5. 'basin' is heights 3, 2, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7. 'switchback' is heights 3, 2, 1, 4, 7, 6, 5. Whichever symbol is present, the seven bar heights are always the seven values 1 to 7 in some order, the middle column is always the height-4 bar, the three left columns always carry the heights 1, 2 and 3 in one order or the other, and the three right columns always carry the heights 5, 6 and 7 in one order or the other. So the total amount of dark ink, the set of bar heights, the panel's size, position and colour, the slats' sizes and colours, and the number of specks are the same whichever symbol is present. The four bars left in the panel fix only the order of one of the two triples, and the three loose slats fix only the order of the other triple, so both the panel and all three slats are needed and neither the panel alone nor the slats alone can decide between two of the four symbols. Which symbol do the seven bars form once the slats have been put back into the empty slots? Answer with exactly one of: basin, crest, ramp, switchback.
